transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, well, I hope I'm not wasting your time, but... I guess what made me come in is that I've just been feeling a little off lately. Nothing too terrible, just... the things that usually make me feel like myself have started feeling really flat. And kind of heavy, if that makes sense? 

Like, I usually love taking these photography walks, and I mentor some kids, which I normally enjoy so much. Even just my day-to-day routine... I'm an executive secretary, so keeping a perfectly clean calendar is usually, you know, my point of pride. But recently, I just... I don't know, I just stopped initiating them. I just haven't been doing any of it. 

Is that... does that sound like the kind of thing I should be bringing up? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
For how long have you been feeling this way?

Um, let me think. I guess... well, if I really look back, it’s probably been about a year and three months? Give or take a little. 

It, um... it started right around the time a family member of mine started having some changes in their health and, well, their behavior. Naturally, I stepped in to help out and took on a lot more of the coordination for them. You know, managing things and just making sure everything was running smoothly. Which I was completely happy to do! I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about helping my family, I love them very much. But I suppose that's when I first started noticing I was dropping some of my own hobbies. 

Does that... does that seem like a reasonable timeline to you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture and not overthinking it.
Have you been experiencing a lack of pleasure in activities that you normally enjoy?

Well, yes, I suppose so. Um, like I mentioned earlier, it's just that the things that usually make me feel like myself—my photography walks, mentoring the kids, even just keeping a perfectly clean calendar for work—they all just started feeling... flat. And kind of heavy. 

I really hope I don't sound ungrateful or lazy, because I know I have a good life. It's just... I stopped initiating those things. I just couldn't seem to find the joy in them anymore, even though I know I should. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question the right way.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the day?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I feel sad, exactly. Or empty. I mean, I definitely don't want you to think I'm sitting around crying all day or anything like that. I'm still getting up and going to work and doing what I need to do. 

It's more just... a little less energy for the fun stuff, I guess? But I wouldn't use words as strong as sad or empty. I try to stay positive, you know? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea of how things are.
Have you been feeling guilty or worthless about anything lately?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I really try to do my best at everything I take on, especially at work and with my family. I don't feel worthless at all. I know I contribute, and I'm proud of the work I do as an executive assistant. 

And as for guilty... well, no, not really. I mean, maybe a tiny bit guilty if I fall behind on an errand or something small, but nothing major. I really try to be a good person and do the right thing, you know? 

I hope that's okay to say. I just wouldn't want you to think I have a low opinion of myself or that I've done something wrong. Does that sound like a normal way to feel?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Um, no, not really. I mean, my clothes still fit the same as they always do. I try to be pretty mindful of what I eat, you know, just to stay healthy and keep up with everything at work. 

I don't think my weight has changed much at all, really. Maybe a pound or two up or down depending on the week, but nothing significant. I try to take good care of myself, so I hope that's a good sign? I mean, it's normal for weight to stay pretty steady if you're keeping a good routine, right?
Have you been having any thoughts about death lately?

Oh, goodness, no. Definitely not. I mean, I really try to focus on the positive things in life, you know? I have a good job, I stay busy... there's just so much to look forward to. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting around having dark thoughts like that. I'm really trying my best to stay focused and upbeat. That's the right way to handle things, isn't it? Just keeping focused on the good stuff?
How much of the day do you feel this lack of energy and flatness?

Well, um, I try really hard not to let it take up the whole day. I push through as best I can. But... I guess it's been enough of the time that it finally made me come in. The things that usually make me feel like myself—like my photography walks, mentoring the kids, even just keeping a really clean calendar at work—they've just started feeling sort of flat and heavy. I realized I just stopped initiating them. 

I'm still doing my best with the important stuff, though! I wouldn't want you to think I'm completely dropping the ball or anything like that. It's just... those extra things take more effort right now. That's a pretty normal reason to come talk to a doctor, right? Just wanting to get back to doing the things you enjoy?
Would you say this feeling of flatness and heaviness is mild, or is it significantly impacting your daily life?

Well, um, I'd say it's... it's mild, mostly. I mean, my work has definitely stayed intact overall. I haven't let anything major slip! I'm still getting the job done. 

It's just... I guess I've missed a few little calendar details here and there, and I've had to double-check some tasks that used to be completely automatic for me. Just to be safe, you know? And, well, I have pulled back from my photography outings and the mentoring... just because I don't feel quite as present or reliable right now, and I want to give them my best. 

But I'm still functioning fine, really! I just want to get back to being 100 percent. That makes sense, doesn't it? Wanting to catch these things early before they become a bigger problem?
How long have you been feeling like you've lost interest in your usual activities?

Well, um... I suppose it's been about a year and three months? Give or take. But there's a really logical reason for it, I promise! It didn't just happen out of nowhere. 

A family member of mine... well, their health and, um, their behavior started changing around then. I needed to step up and take on a lot more coordination for them. I mean, being an executive assistant, organizing things and managing schedules is what I do best, so I was more than happy to take that on. Family comes first! 

It's just that taking on all those extra responsibilities outside of work left me a little drained for my own hobbies. I think anyone would feel a bit tired and lose a little interest in their extra activities when they're managing all that extra family coordination, don't you think? It's just a normal reaction to having a lot on your plate, right?
For how many months have you felt like you've lost interest in your photography walks and mentoring?

Well, um, like I mentioned just a moment ago, it's been right around a year and three months. I guess that sounds like a long time when you say it out loud... but it really all started right when my family member's health and behavior started shifting. 

I just had to step in and take over a lot of the coordination for them, you know? Making sure everything was handled. So it makes perfect sense that my photography and the mentoring had to take a back seat for a while. I mean, anyone would put their hobbies on hold to help family, wouldn't they? It's not like I just gave up on them for no reason. I just prioritized what was most important... that's the right thing to do, isn't it?
Would you say that this feeling of flatness and heaviness is interfering with your daily life more than you initially thought?

Well, um... I guess when you put it like that, maybe a little bit? But really, I wouldn't call it a major interference. I mean, like I said before, my work is still completely intact! I'm still the one keeping the executives on track. 

It's just... well, those little calendar details I mentioned slipping through the cracks, and having to double-check things that I used to do in my sleep. That's just me being thorough, right? Making sure I don't make a real mistake. And yes, I did step back from the photography and the mentoring, but that's just because I want to give them my absolute best, and I didn't feel quite... present enough for that lately. 

But it's not like everything is falling apart! I'm still managing the important things. It's perfectly normal to need a little step back when you're feeling a bit heavy, isn't it? I'm just trying to be responsible about it.
Would you describe the flatness and heaviness you're feeling as something that's affecting your ability to function at work or in your daily responsibilities?

Oh, um... well, I guess it's a lot like what I was just mentioning a second ago. I hope I explained it okay before! But, um, overall, my work has definitely stayed intact. I'm still getting things done. 

It's just... well, I suppose I have missed a couple of very small calendar details lately. Nothing catastrophic, I promise! And I do find myself having to double-check tasks that used to be completely automatic for me. Just to be absolutely sure I'm doing a good job, you know? I want to make sure my executives are supported properly.

And as for my other responsibilities... yes, I have pulled back from the photography outings and my mentoring. I just... I haven't been feeling quite as present or as reliable as I usually am, and I'd really hate to let anyone down. It's better to take a little break than to do a poor job for the people relying on me, right? So I wouldn't say it's stopping me from functioning, just... making me adjust how I do things a little bit. Does that make sense?
Has this feeling of flatness and heaviness been continuous over the past year and three months, or have you had periods where it felt better?

Oh, well... no, it hasn't been completely continuous. I actually do have these stretches where I feel, um, unusually upbeat. Like, really good! Everything just feels like it's clicking perfectly, and I'm totally on top of the schedule. Which is a positive thing, right? It's always nice to have those highly productive days where the heaviness lifts. 

But, um... well, I guess the only thing is... sometimes during those really good stretches, if there's just a tiny change... like, say, someone moving a meeting at the last minute... I can get a little... well, sharp with people. It actually surprises me when it happens, because I always pride myself on being so accommodating and helpful! I just sort of snap, which I feel absolutely terrible about right after. I think it's just because I want everything to run so smoothly for the team, you know? That's just normal office stress, isn't it? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm difficult to work with...
Would you say that most days, you're able to find some pleasure in at least one thing you're doing?

Well, um... I really try to! I mean, I know it's important to stay positive, and I always want to be someone who finds the bright side of things. 

But, honestly, that's kind of the main reason I decided to come in and talk to you. The things that usually make me feel like myself... like taking those photography walks, or spending time mentoring the kids, or even just the satisfaction of keeping a perfectly clean, organized calendar for work... they've all just started feeling so... flat. And heavy. 

I just kind of stopped initiating them. Which I feel awful about! I don't want to be someone who just gives up on their hobbies or the people they help. I'm usually so on top of all of that. But it just takes so much energy lately to even start. That's something we can work on, right? I really want to get back to being my helpful, active self.
Would you say that your lack of interest in activities is something that bothers you a lot?

Oh, yes, it really does. Um, like I was just saying a moment ago, it's honestly the whole reason I finally made the appointment to come in. It bothers me immensely because... well, I just hate that the things that usually make me feel like myself—the photography, the kids I mentor, even just having a perfectly clean calendar at work—they just feel so heavy now. 

And the fact that I've just stopped initiating them... it makes me feel so terribly guilty. I feel like I'm letting people down, which is the absolute last thing I ever want to do. I just really want to get back on track so I can be a good, reliable person for everyone again. That's a good goal to have, right?
Would you say that your lack of interest in activities and feeling of flatness is something that is significantly impacting your relationships with family and friends?

Well, um... I really try my absolute best not to let it affect other people. I always want to be dependable, you know? 

Like, at the office, my work has stayed intact overall, thankfully! I mean... I suppose I have missed a couple of small calendar details here and there, and I've had to double-check tasks that used to just be completely automatic for me. But I always catch it! I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job for the executives. 

But with friends and... well, like I mentioned with the mentoring... I guess I have pulled back from the photography outings and the mentoring sessions. I just... I don't feel as present or as reliable as I normally am right now. And I'd feel terrible if I wasn't giving everyone my best self. It’s better to step back for a little bit rather than be bad company or let them down, right? I just really want to get back to being someone they can count on.
For how many months have you been feeling a lack of interest in the things you usually enjoy?

Well, um... I guess it's been a little while now. Maybe... about a year and three months? 

I really didn't want it to drag on this long, I promise. It actually all started right around the time one of my family members had a... well, a change in their health and behavior, and I had to step up and take on a lot more of the coordination and care for them. 

Which I was happy to do! I always want to be there for my family when they need me. I just think maybe taking on all that extra responsibility kind of... wore me down a little bit more than I realized at the time. It's completely understandable to feel a little drained after something like that, don't you think? I'm just trying to get back to normal now.
Would you say that your lack of interest in activities and feeling of flatness is mild or more pronounced?

Oh, I would definitely say it's on the milder side. Yes, very mild, I promise! I'm really not completely shut down or anything like that. 

It's just... well, like I was mentioning earlier about what finally made me come in... it's just that the things that usually make me feel like myself—the photography walks, mentoring the kids, even keeping that clean calendar at the office—they just started feeling kind of flat and heavy to me. And because of that, I just stopped initiating them. 

But it's really not severe at all, I'm still getting up and trying my absolute best every day. It's just a mild little bump in the road, really. I'm sure it's something we can get sorted out pretty easily, right?
For how many months have you been feeling a lack of interest in the things you usually enjoy, such as photography walks and mentoring?

Oh, sure. Um... yes, like I think I mentioned just a little bit ago, it's been about a year and three months now. 

It all really started right after my family member had those changes in their health and behavior, and I had to step in and take on a lot more of the coordination for their care. I hope I'm explaining that clearly enough for you? I really didn't intend for it to last this long, I promise. I just got so wrapped up in making sure they had everything they needed. It's perfectly normal to need a little time to bounce back after taking on something like that, isn't it?
